_comment: The episode catalogue. One source of truth, read by both the Hub section and the weekly email job, so a title or link is never written down twice. Hand-maintained: add an entry when an episode publishes. `videoUrl` is the SharePoint item URL and stays empty until the file is uploaded -- the email job refuses to send an episode whose videoUrl is empty rather than mailing a dead link.

series.name: Two-Minute Training Tuesday
series.tagline: One tip. One video. Under two minutes. Every Tuesday.

sender._comment: Display name over an address Josh owns -- legitimate, and no Send As grant needed. Switching the address to the Mr. Bean finance alias later DOES need Send As on that mailbox; see distribution/admin-setup.md. Never put the Mr. Bean display name over this address -- that is the spoofing shape that renders as 'on behalf of' and can fail DMARC.

sharePoint._comment: Home as of 2026-08-25: CLC Training on the main site, alongside CLC University, LEHS, IQMS and Paulson -- where staff already look for training. Read access is granted, so videoUrl is a PATH-BASED stream.aspx link: it authorises against each viewer's own permissions, so it survives forwarding and needs no per-item share token. This replaced both the interim TFA library and the ':v:/s/...?e=' share links that library required while it was private to one member. WARNING: a path-based stream link encodes the FILENAME, so renaming or moving a published file breaks it silently -- the Hub keeps rendering a Watch button that lands on an error. Renaming 001 in SharePoint already did this once. Doc.aspx?sourcedoc={guid} is rename-proof but redirects to the folder view for video rather than playing it, so it is not an option here. Treat the published filename as fixed once an episode ships; if it must change, update videoUrl and publishedFileName in the same pass.

episodes.title: Stop using copy and pasting to get a unique list
episodes.summary: Three functions replace the copy, paste, Remove Duplicates, sort routine on any export: =UNIQUE(range), =SORT(UNIQUE(range)), and =FILTER(table, column = criteria).
episodes.publishedFileName: TMTT-001 Stop using copy and pasting to get a unique list.mp4
episodes._comment: The title here is the current wording. The PUBLISHED video's title and recap cards still read 'Stop copying and pasting to get a unique list' -- one word out. Accepted by Josh 2026-08-25: do NOT re-render to fix it. A re-render costs a manual SharePoint upload plus a rename (and a videoUrl update), for a card on screen a few seconds carrying a phrase the narration never speaks.

episodes.title: Data Validation, the basic way and the way that maintains itself
episodes.summary: Every drop-down in Excel is Data Validation. Point Source at a range and it goes stale; point it at =$O$5# and the list maintains itself.
